old: Broker-published figures agree that most value is lost in the early years, but differ on how much.
new: Broker-published figures agree that yachts lose value fastest in their early years, but differ on how much.
reason: Row 15: "Most value is lost in the early years" is wrong against the figures that follow (30 to 50 percent by year five); now says the loss is fastest early.

old: as in the Hill Robinson model
new: as the Hill Robinson model assumes
reason: Row 21: The Hill Robinson case is a design study, not a trading programme; "assumes" keeps that distinction.

new: practice. In it, the owner’s second yacht
reason: Row 24: "The owner" now followed the generic owner of the previous paragraph; "In it" ties it to the case.

old: Test your intended use against these figures.
new: Compare your intended use with these figures.
reason: Row 26: Avoids "Test ... tests" in consecutive sentences.
Row 36: Referent is the management company (singular) now the sentence names it as subject.

old: In most, charter income offsets part of the cost of ownership but does not cover it; the profitable exception assumes
new: In three of the four, charter income at best matches running cost; the profitable exception, a design study, assumes
reason: Row 49: "In most ... does not cover it" misdescribes the 48m case, which broke even; states what the four cases show.

new: Slot dates as published by September 2026.
reason: Row 119: "As published by September 2026." was a fragment with no subject.

old: contains a dual-agency clause under which both parties consent to dual agency in advance.
reason: Row 148: New wording duplicated the next sentence ("Signing the standard form means ... already agreed"); the next sentence carries the advance consent.

old: widely known in the trade but rarely disclosed
new: widely known in the trade but not always disclosed
reason: Row 156: "Rarely disclosed" is a new unsupported frequency claim; "not always" keeps the sense of "open secret".

old: The adviser runs the project for the owner:
new: The adviser acts for the owner across the project:
reason: Row 169: "Runs the project" sat awkwardly with the next sentence saying the role is not a project manager.

old: Sales are agreed later, in the weeks after the viewing,
new: Most sales are agreed later, in the weeks after the show,
reason: Row 218: Qualified the generalisation (Christie sold two off a show) and tied it to the boat show of the preceding quote.

old: and both are often settled in a hurry at closing
new: and both can end up being settled in a hurry at closing
reason: Row 219: "Often" hardened the original "can end up being"; original modality restored.

old: secured by nothing more than the contract and the payment record
new: backed by the contract and the payment record
reason: Row 295: "Nothing more" hardened the claim and ignores a refund guarantee where one exists (item 2).

old: and responsible for the project at senior level
new: and responsible for the project as a whole
reason: Row 299: "At senior level" is vague; next sentence already says "above the day-to-day".

old: in the industry. Such arrangements are common.
new: in the industry, which was true as far as it went.
reason: Row 320: "Such arrangements are common" lost the original point (true only in a narrow sense) and added a bare generalisation.

old: the change-order clause had allowed the yard about EUR 5.2 m in margin across the build
new: the change-order clause had left the yard free to set its own margin on about EUR 13 m of variations
reason: Row 327: EUR 5.2 m is total variation margin; the case itself says the calculation does not show how much was avoidable, so the clause is not credited with all of it.

old: The seller needs the same advisers as the buyer.
new: The seller needs the same kind of advisers as the buyer.
reason: Row 364: "The same advisers" could read as the same people; the next sentence means the seller’s own lawyer and adviser.

old: Projected refit cost as a percentage of pre-refit market value, compared with
new: Projected refit cost, as a percentage of pre-refit market value, compared with
reason: Row 416: Commas make the cost, not the percentage, the thing compared with the cost of selling.
